content: {"summary":"After the 19 Mar 2025 zone push to internal‑dns‑01 removed the database record used by orders‑api, CoreDNS sometimes queried the updated server and returned NXDOMAIN while the other server still had the record, causing intermittent failures. The missing record was re‑added and a corrected zone file was pushed to internal‑dns‑01 at 15:38; once the cluster cache refreshed, all lookups succeeded.","likely_cause":"Missing DNS record in the zone file on internal‑dns‑01 after the March 2025 zone push","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The zone push removed the required record on internal‑dns‑01, causing CoreDNS cache to sometimes return NXDOMAIN and sometimes the correct address.","evidence_ids":["INC-0025#0","INC-0025#1"],"quote":"Only internal-dns-01 served the new file, so a cache period that happened to land there came back NXDOMAIN"},{"text":"The record was re‑added and a corrected zone file pushed at 15:38; after the cache turned over lookups succeeded consistently.","evidence_ids":["INC-0025#2","INC-0025#3"],"quote":"Once the cluster cache turned over, lookups from orders-api-02 resolved every time; the last failed one was logged at 15:38"}],"next_checks":["Verify that zone pushes are applied to all DNS servers simultaneously","Monitor CoreDNS cache TTL and ensure cache turnover after pushes","Add post‑push validation queries for critical records","Implement alert on NXDOMAIN spikes for prod.internal names"]}
